medfit Model Syntax

Source: R/sem-syntax-help.R
medfit-syntax.Rd

The model syntax read by fit_sem() and by fit_mediation(engine = "sem") (the sem engine; "native" is the legacy spelling). It is a lavaan-style core plus two extensions, each marked "medfit extension" below. One statement per line (or separated by ;).

Missing-data scope

The general syntax below describes the default listwise path. The separate bounded fit_sem(missing = "fiml", fixed_x = FALSE) option accepts only three numeric observed variables in simple mediation with a free or exactly zero direct path and free intercepts. General constraints, definitions, starts, bounds, latent variables, products and factors are not supported for FIML. See fit_sem() for all settings and downstream limits.

Core statements

StatementMeaning
y ~ x1 + x2regression of y on x1 and x2
f =~ y1 + y2 + y3latent variable f measured by the indicators
y1 ~~ y2covariance; y1 ~~ y1 a variance
y ~ x + m + x:mproduct term: the observed variable x * m as a regressor (see Product terms)
y ~ a*xlabel the path a; equal labels are one parameter
y ~ 0.5*xfix the path at 0.5
y ~ start(0.3)*x, lower(0)*, upper(1)*starting value, lower and upper bound
a == b, a + b == 1, cp == a*bequality constraint on labels; may be nonlinear
a < b, a > 0inequality constraint; label < number is a bound
ab := a*bdefined parameter, with a delta-method standard error

Constraints may be nonlinear in the labels (cp == a*b, a*b == 0.1, a*b > 0.1, ab > 0 with ab := a*b), solved with the Jacobian recomputed at every point; a model with one tries every start and keeps the best accepted solution, warning when the starts disagree. For such a model the residual variances that appear in a nonlinear row get a lower bound of 1e-4 times their natural unit (the variable's variance), because a step to a negative variance is outside the row's domain; the fit warns when a bound is active, and a residual variance below that bound (an R-squared above 0.9999) is not fitted exactly. The model without the nonlinear rows is fitted first: its estimate, and copies of it with the signs of the regression paths in the rows flipped (a product constraint cannot change sign along its surface, so each sign pattern is its own branch), are extra starts, and a feasible reference estimate is never replaced by a worse accepted fit. Models without a nonlinear row are not affected. One nonzero-product equality (a*b == 0.1, including a finite nonzero constant multiplier and definition aliases) has a separate search for each sign of its two distinct free labels. Each required sign branch must be accepted or excluded by its bounds; an unresolved branch stops the fit. Multiple product equalities, repeated factors and another constraint involving either factor retain local search. The internal coverage record distinguishes charted branches from local search, not global from local optima; see fit_sem(). A product of labels set to zero (a*b == 0, b1*b2*b3 == 0) is instead solved exactly: one linear fit per factor (a == 0, b == 0), keeping the smallest discrepancy; if a branch cannot be fitted, fit_sem() stops with a medfit_error_no_convergence error instead of returning the best of the others; the error carries the outcome ledger of every branch as $ledger (see fit_sem()). A sum of products (a1*b1 + a2*b2 == 0) has no exact reduction, so it is best-effort: the fit is the best of the starts tried, a disagreement warning means a better optimum may exist, and n_starts raises the number of starts. Constrained standard errors use the active tangent space: observed information includes nonlinear constraint curvature, while expected information retains its Fisher definition. Active inequalities and bounds, including solver variance floors, give a local tangent approximation rather than the full boundary sampling distribution. See fit_sem() and the Methods and Formulas article for details. Labels used in a constraint or a definition must be defined in the model. A constraint with no free parameter is an error. Exogenous variables are given free variances and covariances, as lavaan does with fixed.x = FALSE. An exogenous variable named in any ~~ statement is left out of that pairing: its variance and the covariances the model writes are kept, and its covariances with the other exogenous variables are 0 unless written (lavaan does the same). fixed_x = TRUE (or a vector of names) in fit_sem() fixes the moments of the selected ones at the sample values instead, as fixed.x = TRUE does. Unlike lavaan, which keeps an explicit x ~~ x or x ~ 1 free under fixed.x = TRUE and lets the degrees of freedom move, medfit stops with an error when the model has a statement on a selected variable's moments. Any intercept statement (y ~ 1, or 1 as a term: y ~ 1 + x) turns the mean structure on and frees every observed intercept the model does not write, as lavaan does; y ~ 0*1 then restricts the mean of y to 0 (one degree of freedom), and meanstructure = TRUE in fit_sem() turns it on without any statement, and a product term (x:m, see Product terms) always turns it on. A latent variable's mean is fixed at 0; a free latent ~1 is an error. A repeated 1 for one variable is an error. A variable cannot appear on both sides of ~ or =~ (y ~ y), and a path, a (co)variance or an intercept takes one row: a repeated y ~ x is an error, not a second row that competes for the label.

Factor covariates

A factor, character or logical column named on a regression's right side is replaced by one 0/1 dummy per non-reference level, named <column>_<level> (g with levels a, b, c gives g_b and g_c). The reference level is the first factor level; a character column sorts in the C locale, so the result does not depend on the session locale. A logical column gives one dummy, <column>_TRUE. Dummies are built from the full column before rows with missing values are dropped, and a missing value in the factor drops the row once. tidy() and the parameter table show the dummies by name, and the fit's data holds the dummies, not the factor.

LimitMessage (starts with, or contains)
An ordered factor"is an ordered factor"
A factor with one level"has only one level"
A level that makes an invalid name"makes the invalid name"
A dummy that is already a column"is already a column of data"
A label, fixed value, start or bound on a factor (b*g)"expands to"
A constraint that names the factor (g == 0)"is a categorical column"
A product of two factors"both sides are categorical columns"
A dummy with no variation in the rows used"is constant in the rows the fit uses"
A factor as the outcome or a mediator"must be numeric"
A factor as treatment or mediator in extract_mediation()"is a factor in the model"

A label goes on one dummy: b*g_b works, b*g stops, and a constraint names the label (b == 0), never the factor. A bootstrap that refits from raw data re-expands the factor in each resample, so a level missing from a character column's resample changes the reference level. g:m expands to g_b:m and g_c:m, each a product term under the rules below. fixed_x = "g" fixes every dummy of g, and a dummy name fixes one. A factor covariate in the mediator equation enters the four-way covariate means through its dummies; a factor treatment or mediator is not supported (recode a two-level factor as a 0/1 numeric column), and the four-way route refuses a g:m product because its effects differ by level.

Product terms

x:m is the product of two observed variables, written with no spaces, on the right side of a regression (y ~ x + m + x:m). As in lavaan, the product is an observed exogenous variable: the engine builds the column x * m from data after listwise deletion, with a free variance, free covariances with the other exogenous variables and (the mean structure is on) a free mean. The likelihood does not change. x:m and m:x are one term, stored and printed under the canonical name, the two names sorted in the C locale (m:x); the coefficient is named y~m:x, or by its label (b*x:m labels the whole product). extract_mediation() finds the treatment-by-mediator product through the same name and returns the four-way decomposition; centering the mediator moves the split between the controlled direct effect and the reference interaction, not the natural effects.

A column in data named m:x or x:m is used only if it equals x * m on the rows kept; otherwise the fit stops. A product term turns the mean structure on, and meanstructure = FALSE is then an error. A coefficient equals the equation-wise least-squares estimate inside the class below, and the sandwich covariance (se_type = "sandwich") is the standard-error choice, because a product is not normal; the engine warns once when it is not used. fixed_x includes the product columns.

LimitMessage (starts with, or contains)
A space around :"a product ':' needs a variable name on each side, written without spaces (x:m)"
x:x"of a variable with itself is not supported"
x:m:w"a three-way or higher product"
Product as a left side (x:m ~ y, x:m ~~ y)"cannot be a left side"
Product in =~"is only valid on the right side of a regression"
Product inside a constraint or :="not inside the expression"
A latent variable in a product"products with latent variables are not supported in this version"
y ~ x:m + m:x (one product twice in an equation)"are the same product (canonical name"
A factor that is the target or downstream of it (y ~ x + x:y)"(rule 8: no outcome-derived regressors)"
A loop of regressions"The model is not recursive"
A residual covariance between outcomes (m1 ~~ m2)"cannot have a residual covariance (rule 9)"
A label shared by two rows"is used on more than one parameter"
A fixed coefficient (0.3*x, 0*x)"has a fixed coefficient (rule 9)"
A bound (lower(0)*x)"has a bound (rule 9"
==, < or > naming a coefficient label"names the coefficient label"
A fixed, shared or constrained intercept"(rule 9, intercept clause"
meanstructure = FALSE with a product"meanstructure = FALSE, but the model has a product term"
A column m:x in data that is not x * m"is not the product of"
A product input that is not numeric, factor, character or logical (a date)"needs numeric variables"
information = "expected", endogenous factor"with a product of an endogenous variable"
anova() or mbco_sem() on such a fit"is not available for ... a model with a product term"
Another product on the treatment or mediator, in extract_mediation()"does not support the product"
AIC() or BIC() on fits with different observed variables"different observed variables"
A product of two categorical columns (g:h)"both sides are categorical columns"
fixed_x naming a column that appears only inside products"appears only inside products"
A product in a modifier (y ~ a:b*x)"malformed modifier"
Four-way on a native fit without the treatment-by-mediator product"needs the treatment-by-mediator product"
extract_mediation(interaction = ) that is not a : product"must be the product written with :"
extract_mediation(interaction = ) that is not treatment by mediator"is not the product of the treatment"

Each error has one of these classes and also the class medfit_error_product; the message is the reason, so a handler can match the class and a reader the message. The warning that the model test is not valid (below) has the class medfit_warning_product_modeltest.

ClassRaised for
medfit_error_product_syntaxspacing, x:x, three-way, left side, =~, constraint expression
medfit_error_product_latenta latent variable in a product
medfit_error_product_duplicateone product twice in an equation
medfit_error_product_outcome_regressorrule 8
medfit_error_product_recursivea loop of regressions
medfit_error_product_residual_covarianceresidual covariance between outcomes
medfit_error_product_shared_labela label on two rows
medfit_error_product_fixed_coefficienta fixed coefficient
medfit_error_product_boundan inline bound
medfit_error_product_constrainta constraint names a coefficient label
medfit_error_product_intercepta fixed, shared or constrained intercept
medfit_error_product_meanstructuremeanstructure = FALSE
medfit_error_product_columna data column that is not the product
medfit_error_product_nonnumerica non-numeric product input
medfit_error_product_informationinformation = "expected", endogenous factor
medfit_error_product_modeltestanova() or mbco_sem()
medfit_error_product_observedAIC() or BIC() across observed variables
medfit_error_product_extractextract_mediation() refusals

Rules 8 and 9 are checked on the parsed table, so they need no data. Rule 8 rejects a regressor built from the outcome (it is correlated with the equation's error); rule 9 names what is not yet supported with products, and the same model works without the product. The covariance that completion would add between two pure outcomes is fixed at 0 in a product model, with one note. Products of observed variables only: a product with a latent variable, x:x and three-way products are not supported.

The global chi-square is not valid when a factor of a product is itself a regression target (the model treats the product as exogenous although it is a function of that variable) or when the exogenous (co)variance block is restricted. glance() then reports chi-square, df and p-value as NA with a note, anova() and mbco_sem() refuse, and expected information is refused for an endogenous product; logLik(), AIC and BIC stay defined, but those of a fit with a product are not comparable with those of a fit without one, so AIC(fit_a, fit_b), BIC(), anova() and mbco_sem() refuse such a pair. A product of exogenous variables with the block free keeps the ordinary test.

Two-level models (experimental)

A two-level model of observed variables is written in level: blocks and fitted with fit_sem(model, data, cluster = "<cluster column>"). level: 1 and level: within open the within block; level: 2, level: between and level: <cluster column> (as lavaan writes it) open the between block. Every row belongs to a block, each level appears once, and level 1 comes first. A variable named in level: 1 rows (a within variable) must also appear in level: 2 rows and must vary within clusters; a variable named only in level: 2 rows is a cluster-level variable and must be constant within each cluster. The same label at both levels is an equality constraint across levels. Paths have fixed slopes (no random slopes), and the between part of each within variable is a latent cluster mean. Level-2 variances are fitted without a floor: an inadmissible solution (a negative variance or a non-positive-definite implied covariance at either level) is the error medfit_error_twolevel_inadmissible, which carries the fit (fit) and its outcome ledger (ledger). Unset fixed_x means FALSE and unset meanstructure means TRUE on this route.

LimitMessage (starts with, or contains)
cluster = without level: blocks"is given but the model has no level: blocks"
level: blocks without cluster ="the model uses level: blocks but cluster is not given"
A cluster column that is not in data"is not a column of data"
Missing values in the cluster column"has missing values; drop those rows first"
Fewer than two clusters"has fewer than 2 clusters"
More than two levels"the model has more than two levels"
An unknown level name (level: school with another cluster column)"malformed level line"
A row before the first level: line"has statements before the first level: line"
A level written twice"appears more than once"
level: 2 without level: 1"rows but no level: 1 block"
A variable named only in level: 1 rows"every level-1 variable also needs a level: 2 row"
A within variable constant within every cluster"a cluster-level variable belongs only in level: 2 rows"
A level: 2-only variable that varies within a cluster"must be constant within each cluster"
Latent variables (=~)"latent variables (=~) are not supported in a two-level model"
A product term (x:m)"a product term (x:m) is not supported in a two-level model"
weights"weights are not supported in a two-level model"
missing = "fiml""missing = ... incomplete rows are dropped (listwise)"
Nonlinear constraints (not a_w*b_w == a_b*b_b)"nonlinear constraints (including a product of labels"
An explicit fixed_x = TRUE or a name vector"a two-level model takes fixed_x = FALSE only"
meanstructure = FALSE"meanstructure = FALSE is refused"
information = "expected""information = ... is not supported in a two-level model; use"
An inadmissible solution"the two-level solution is inadmissible"
compare_lr() on the fit"is not available for a native two-level fit yet"
mbco_sem() with paths from different levels"tests a product of paths at one level of a two-level fit"

mbco_sem(fit, "a_w", "b_w") and mbco_sem(fit, "a_b", "b_b") test the indirect effect at one level: the minimum likelihood ratio over the refits with each labeled path set to 0, referred to chi-square(1), as for a single-level fit. The test is conservative when both paths are zero, and it is not a test of the between-minus-within contrast. The result adds level and n_clusters; see mbco_sem().

extract_mediation() on the fit returns a TwoLevelMediationData, the same class as the lavaan two-level adapter gives, with @source "native". glance() reports df, the total log likelihood, nobs, n_clusters and the cluster-size range; chisq and p_value are NA with a note, because the engine fits no saturated two-level model. The model page "Two-level mediation (1-1-1)" has a worked example.

Defaults changed in 0.15.0

Since medfit 0.15.0 an unset fixed_x means the exogenous observed variables (as lavaan's fixed.x = TRUE) and an unset meanstructure means TRUE, so every observed intercept is free without a ~1 statement. Against 0.14.x the parameter count, logLik(), AIC(), BIC() and the parameter names move; the structural estimates and their standard errors did not move on the cases measured. A variable a ~~ or ~1 statement names is left free (message class medfit_message_fixed_x_lenient) instead of the error an explicit fixed_x = TRUE gives. To keep the 0.14.x results, pass fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL. The 0.14.x options(medfit.native_defaults) opt-in no longer has any effect. fit_sem() has the details.

medfit extensions

  • Comma shorthand (medfit extension). A comma-separated left side expands to one statement per name: y1, y2 ~ x means y1 ~ x and y2 ~ x. Commas on the right side are not supported; use +. lavaan reads y1, y2 ~ x differently: it silently keeps only y2. A model copied between the two packages can therefore change meaning without an error.

  • CONSTRAINT(...) (medfit extension). A constraint line may be written CONSTRAINT(a == b), equivalent to the bare a == b. The keyword is case-sensitive and starts the statement, one pair of parentheses encloses the whole constraint, it holds exactly one comparison, and no text follows the closing parenthesis.

Expressions

Both sides of a constraint and the right side of a definition are arithmetic expressions in the labels, with + - * / ^, parentheses, finite numbers, and the functions exp, log, log10, sqrt, abs, min, max, sin, cos, tan, pnorm and qnorm. Anything else is rejected with the construct named.

See also

fit_sem(), SEMFit

Examples

# \donttest{
# Labeled paths and a defined parameter
fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment\nab := a*b",
  data = mediation_demo, fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL
)@defined
#>   name expr       est         se
#> 1   ab  a*b 0.3253207 0.08016376

# Comma shorthand: one left-hand side per name
coef(fit_sem(
  "mediator1, mediator2 ~ treatment\noutcome ~ mediator1 + mediator2 + treatment",
  data = mediation_demo
))[1:3]
#> mediator1~treatment mediator2~treatment   outcome~mediator1 
#>           0.4559961           0.2879985           0.5202186 

# An equality constraint, written with the CONSTRAINT() keyword
coef(fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + treatment\nCONSTRAINT(a == b)",
  data = mediation_demo
))[c("a", "b")]
#>         a         b 
#> 0.6673103 0.6673103 
# }
